title: Unbounded derived sections agree with localized-site derived sections
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in a common universe containing its objects, arrows, covering families and coefficient values [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ for its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, put $\mathcal O_W=\mathcal O|_W$, and let $j_W^*$ denote sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Use unbounded cochain derived categories and total right derived functors computed by K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$, let $R\Gamma(W,K)$ be derived evaluation at $W$, followed by forgetting scalars, and let $R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K)$ be derived evaluation at the final object $\mathrm{id}_W$ of the slice, also followed by forgetting scalars. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, natural in $K$, $$R\Gamma(W,K)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K).$$ For any K-injective representative $I$ of $K$, this isomorphism is represented by the degreewise identity $I(W)=(I|_W)(\mathrm{id}_W)$. In particular, for every integer $q$, $$H^qR\Gamma(W,K)\cong H^qR\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,j_W^*K).$$ No boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: The site and its slice are small in the common universe. Apply the existing proved source theorem SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Abelian) on each. This is the common-universe special case of the ring-sheaf Grothendieck property appearing in the statement; no independent-universe transport theorem is needed. The proved Grothendieck-category K-injective-resolution instance supplies all resolution hypotheses of the total right derived functors in the statement. Restriction is additive directly by sectionwise extensionality. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], its termwise functor preserves K-injective complexes. Package this as PreservesKInjectiveComplexes.

proof.text: By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], restriction followed by evaluation at id_W and forgetting scalars is definitionally evaluation at W and forgetting scalars, on both objects and morphisms. This remains the literal identity on termwise complexes and differentials, as sectionComplexIdentity records.

source.place: Tag 0D6F proof, identity of the two section complexes

proof.text: Apply the existing closed unbounded composition theorem [lem-fin-kinjective-derived-composition] to restriction F and localized evaluation G, with H=F composed with G and the identity comparison, using its underlying rightDerivedFunctorCompIso. This gives the required natural isomorphism because F composed with G is definitionally evaluation at W. For normalization, evaluate rightDerivedNatTrans_app, the universal factorization equation defining the composition comparison, on the homotopy quotient of a K-injective I. Its right-hand side is the composite derived unit: the G-unit followed by G applied to the F-unit. Both units are invertible since I and F(I) are K-injective. Cancel the units, and use naturality of the comparison along quotientCompQhIso.inv. Expanding rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso cancels the intermediate quotientCompQhIso and its inverse, giving precisely the equation with Q of sectionComplexIdentity. Finally apply homologyFunctor in any integer degree to the component of this natural isomorphism. These are purely categorical unit and isomorphism calculations and impose no boundedness condition.

lean.statement: theorem unboundedSectionsLocalization (W : C) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} (R.over W))] : ∃ e : derivedEvaluation R W ≅ derivedRestriction R W ⋙ derivedEvaluation (R.over W) (Over.mk (𝟙 W)), (∀ (I : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u} R) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective], e.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫ (derivedEvaluation (R.over W) (Over.mk (𝟙 W))).map ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} R W).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso I).hom ≫ ((evaluation (R.over W) (Over.mk (𝟙 W))).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso ((restrictComplex R W).obj I)).hom = ((evaluation R W).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso I).hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (sectionComplexIdentity R W I).hom) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{u} R)) (q : ℤ), Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} q).obj ((derivedEvaluation R W).obj K) ≅ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} q).obj ((derivedEvaluation (R.over W) (Over.mk (𝟙 W))).obj ((derivedRestriction R W).obj K))))
lean.note: Natural isomorphism of total right derived functors, normalized on every K-injective representative by Q of the literal section-complex identity. All integer cohomology degrees are included. The common-universe hypothesis is encoded by C, its arrows, ring values and module values in u; localization Hom universes w and z are independent. The additional already landed statement dependency supplies Grothendieck abelianness for arbitrary ring sheaves, without imposing commutativity.
